Logical operators and short-circuiting

&& returns the first falsy operand or the last operand; || returns the first truthy operand or the
last operand. Both can skip evaluating the right operand.

Interview question: Do && and || always return Boolean values?
Answer: No. They return one of their operands and may short-circuit.
Remember: AND stops at falsy; OR stops at truthy.
